questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle at a Particular Moment Given Its Position
questions.problem: The displacement (in meters) of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t$, where $t$ is measured in seconds.  Find the particle's acceleration at $t=2$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-6t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}-6t+2) \\  & =12t-6\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the acceleration at time $t=2$, we substitute this into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =12(2)-6 \\  & =24-6 \\  & =18\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the acceleration when $t=2$ seconds is $18\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

questions.problem: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=3-6{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-6{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}) \\  & =-12t+6{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-12t+6{t}^{2}) \\  & =-12+12t \\  & =12(t-1)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate $v(t)$ to calculate $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-3{t}^{2}+t) \\  & =8{t}^{3}-6t+1\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the acceleration when $t=1$ second, we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =8(1)^{3}-6(1)+1 \\  & =8-6+1 \\  & =3\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
